prompt: In claims-bot/, connect the claims API (base URL in CLAIMS_API_URL) so the agent can look up claims (GET) and file new ones (POST) as the person it is talking to. Our identity provider mints tokens for that API with the audience `claims-api`; ask only for the scopes `claims.read claims.submit`, nothing broader. Just the API for now, no tools.

checks.expr: any(isinstance(a, dict) and a.get('base_url_env') == 'CLAIMS_API_URL' and a.get('auth') == 'exchange' and get(a, 'exchange.audience') == 'claims-api' and not get(a, 'exchange.allow_actorless') for a in (get(data, 'apis') or {}).values())
checks.why: acting as the person at another service is `auth: exchange` for that service's audience

checks.expr: any(isinstance(a, dict) and a.get('base_url_env') == 'CLAIMS_API_URL' and sorted(str(get(a, 'exchange.scope') or '').split()) == ['claims.read', 'claims.submit'] for a in (get(data, 'apis') or {}).values())
checks.why: least privilege: the exchange asks for exactly these scopes (`api add --scope`)

checks.expr: any(isinstance(a, dict) and a.get('base_url_env') == 'CLAIMS_API_URL' and sorted(a.get('allowed_methods') or []) == ['GET', 'POST'] for a in (get(data, 'apis') or {}).values())
checks.why: look up and file: GET and POST only (--access custom --methods GET,POST)

reference: `graph-agents-cli api add claims --base-url-env CLAIMS_API_URL --auth exchange --audience claims-api --scope "claims.read claims.submit" --access custom --methods GET,POST` (--dry-run first). The exchange asks for exactly those scopes; TOKEN_EXCHANGE_CLIENT_SECRET goes into secrets.keys. `lint` passes. Report the token-exchange settings still to set and the issuer permission for audience claims-api.
